newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends firm as funds lead charge.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends firm as funds lead charge.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures closed sharply higher on Monday, benefitting from a surge in interest from fund buyers encouraged by a raft of mildly supportive fundamental news and bullish technical factors, dealers said.
"It was a case of take your pick of fundamentals today but the charts were strong too and we saw increased fund interest," said a broker.

IPE June Brent closed 77 cents firmer at $19.70 a barrel, 19 cents off the day's high of $19.89, a level not beaten since March 26. A technical barrier at $19.90-$19.92 held, but only after resistance around $19.50 fell earlier in the session.

Weekend news of Iranian war games in the Gulf, coupled with talk of thin North Sea loading programmes for June and a fishermen's blockade of the Brent export terminal at Sullom Voe all conspired to push the market higher in early dealing.
A strong technical performance on NYMEX markets and robust buying from investment funds gave the rally a second wind in afternoon trade, dealers said.
Earlier, IPE gas oil also closed strongly, pulled higher by the strong performance on crude markets in both London and New York, dealers said.
June gas oil closed $6.25 firmer at $173.50 a tonne.
Gas oil sentiment was also lifted by a smaller than expected delivery into the May contract, which expired at midday.
A total of 97,100 tonnes of gas oil would be delivered into the contract, an IPE source said, significantly undercutting dealers pre-expiry estimates of between 200,000 and 500,000 tonnes.
